article.title: A Percentage Needs a Starting Point
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: A percentage can sound clear while hiding the most important information: the starting point. Imagine a report that says sales increased by 20 percent. If sales were $100 before, they are now $120. But if a satisfaction score rises from 20 percent to 40 percent, it increased by 20 percentage points and doubled in relative terms. These are different statements. The denominator matters too. Suppose 100 customers buy a product out of 10,000 eligible customers. The conversion rate is 1 percent. If the eligibility rule changes and only 5,000 customers remain in the denominator, the same 100 purchases produce a 2 percent conversion rate. The percentage doubled even though the number of purchases did not change. This is why analysts should report the baseline, numerator, denominator, and comparison period whenever possible. Relative changes can be useful because they show proportional movement, but they can make small absolute changes look dramatic when the baseline is tiny. Percentage-point changes are often clearer when comparing rates. A good sentence might say, “Conversion increased from 1.0 percent to 1.2 percent, a gain of 0.2 percentage points or 20 percent relative.” That wording gives readers both views. Time also matters. A monthly rate should not be compared casually with an annual rate, and a rate calculated from a filtered population may not be comparable with one calculated before the filter changed. Percentages are not misleading by themselves. Problems appear when the reference point is missing. Before reacting to a large percentage, ask: compared with what, out of how many, and over what period? Analysts should define the population, observation window, decision rule, and operational constraint before interpreting the metric. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文強調分析結果必須放回正確的 baseline、母體、segment、decision cost 與資料生成機制中理解。百分比、總體 KPI、model threshold 或部署後的新資料，都可能因分母、selection、population mix 或舊 policy 而改變含義。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：分析結果はbaseline、母集団、segment、decision cost、data generating mechanismと結び付けて解釈する必要がある。percentage、集計KPI、model threshold、deployment後のdataは、分母、selection、population mix、過去policyによって意味が変わり得る。
